launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-camera
description: Diego's Cloud Camera — our own signed build of GrapheneOS Camera. Modern CameraX (photo, video, QR/barcode scan, timer, zoom/exposure bars, in-app gallery), pure Kotlin/Java, no NDK, no Play Services. Vendored upstream tree renamed onto cld.camera so it coexists with an officially-signed GrapheneOS Camera on the same device.

voice._doc: Offline voice-shutter configuration, data-driven from this file. The trigger word is read at build time into BuildConfig so the shutter can never drift from what is declared here. A camera listens only when the user opts in.

_doc_mode: Hub-less single-fork app, exactly like ac_cloud-gallery: there is no hub module and no IPC contract — the single forks.<key> entry IS the app, built through the engine's step_build_fork machinery.

modules._doc: Task #461 — the ONE shared image-scan engine (ZXing barcode decode + ML Kit OCR + typed-payload parsing), consumed BY REFERENCE from ab_cloud-libs-shared exactly like cloud-drive and cloud-gallery. Declared here so the ship workflow watches it and the publish gate hashes it: a fix to the shared engine must trigger a camera rebuild, not silently ride along or skip one.

libs:ml-l-sound._doc: #798 the CONTRACT half of the fleet's sound identification (ISoundEngine wire, SoundEngine client, sound.json), shared with Cloud Calc: Identify's Sound mode and /api/sound/classify. YAMNet runs in Cloud-Lib-Ml-L-Sound-Yamnet.apk, which this app binds after a contract handshake and never compiles (a `contract` lib, no L4 edge).

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership: core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission. Declared so a core change rebuilds camera instead of shipping a stale mesh member.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>); not linked directly. Listed so its changes also trigger a rebuild.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:ml-l-vision-mlkit._doc: #1533 the shared on-device vision toolkit (Detection, ObjectDetector, DetectionOverlayView, FrameMapping with rotation and mirroring, AnalysisGate / AnalyzerLifecycle) compiled BY REFERENCE: the Objects and VR pages use it, other apps can too.

libs:bottomnav._doc: #868 the fleet's bottom island + page-tab strips + NavDecl, shared BY REFERENCE: ui/ModeNav.kt draws the camera mode switcher with them (the hand-rolled snapping TabLayout is gone).

libs:ui-icons._doc: #1160 the nav icon catalog (name to ImageVector, tinted or brand): every nav glyph of every app, shared BY REFERENCE; libs:bottomnav depends on it.

libs:ui-nav-bars._doc: #1352 Configs ▸ General and ▸ About (fleetconfigs): FleetConfigsActivity, started from this app's own menu. Shared BY REFERENCE.

libs:theme-background._doc: libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency (the page background); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path.

libs:perms._doc: #1360/#1352 libs:ui-nav-bars' `api` dependency: Configs ▸ General ▸ Perms is libs:perms' AppPermsSection, first run asks every never-asked grant.

android._doc_version: version_name mirrors upstream's release tag ('93'); app/build.gradle.kts reads it. version_code is the DECLARED code the fleet manifest carries; the APK's own versionCode is the fleet build stamp (#789: 3,000,000 + minutes since 2026-01-01), because a constant 93 never moved across our builds.

_doc_abi_filters: EMPTY ON PURPOSE. GrapheneOS Camera has no native code (no externalNativeBuild, no JNI) so it produces ONE universal APK that runs on every ABI — unlike ac_cloud-gallery, which needs an ABI build matrix because ReFra compiles libheif/libde265.

signing._doc: ONE shared Cloud-constellation signing key for ALL Android apps. KEY LOCATION: Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/release.jks (OU=Cloud Constellation) + Shared/Providers/D_TOOLS-DEVICES/d2-android/signing.secrets.yaml.

camera._doc: Plural 'forks.<key>' map — same shape as ac_cloud-gallery/build.json::forks.'gallery'. Exactly one key because this app IS the fork (no separate thin hub), matching top-level mode:'single-app'.
camera.tracker_dir_note: VENDORED: the upstream tree sits at the app root (no .git), so materialize-fork returns early and build-fork uses the committed source as-is. upstream_repo/pinned_tag/pinned_commit are provenance; re-vendoring means cloning a newer tag by hand and re-applying the cld.camera rename.
camera._doc_pinned_tag: Verified 2026-08-31 via the GitHub tags API: GrapheneOS/Camera tags are bare release numbers (93, 92, 91, 90, ...). 93 is the newest. Vendored from that exact tag; pinned_commit is its tip.
camera._doc_license: Confirmed via GitHub's license API (spdx_id MIT) and the vendored LICENSE file, which is kept verbatim at ac_cloud-camera/LICENSE.

build._doc: Plain single-module gradle build with upstream's own wrapper (Gradle 9.6.1) and AGP 9.3.1. No product flavors and no ABI dimension, so ONE task serves every device — hence no gradle_task_by_abi map. NO 'signing' key on purpose: upstream's signingConfigs.release only activates when a rootProject keystore.properties is readable, and that block also builds a 'play' config that hard-casts keystoreProperties["uploadKeyAlias"], so writing a 4-key keystore.properties would NPE at configure time. We instead let gradle emit app-release-unsigned.apk and let the engine's _enforce_signature zipalign + apksigner it with the ONE shared constellation key — which is the real signing guarantee anyway, since _enforce_signature overwrites whatever gradle produced.

camera.comment: GrapheneOS Camera, renamed onto cld.camera. Chosen over Open Camera because it is actively maintained, CameraX-based and builds on a stock GHA runner with no NDK.
camera._doc_rename: applicationId AND namespace moved app.grapheneos.camera → cld.camera, the java source packages moved app/src/{main,androidTest}/java/app/grapheneos/camera → .../cld/camera, and every custom-view class name inside res/layout (app.grapheneos.camera.ui.*) followed. The rename is REQUIRED for coexistence: the user may install official GrapheneOS Camera builds, and two APKs cannot share an applicationId. Upstream declares no FileProvider authority and no shortcuts.xml, so there is nothing else keyed off the old id. The visible label is 'Cloud Camera' via the release buildType's resValue app_name.

release._doc: Per-APK distribution, same data-driven pattern as ac_cloud-gallery::release. {sha} → git short sha, {version_name} → android.version_name.

ghcr._doc: ORAS push as an OCI artifact (the APK is a blob, not a container). The layer's org.opencontainers.image.title annotation comes from the pushed filename, so publish-fork pushes release.artifact.release — the Constellation AppStore reads that title to name the download.

gh_release._doc: Rolling GH release 'latest', overwritten on every main push, so /releases/latest/download/Cloud-Camera.apk stays a stable URL. Consumed by aa_cloud-superapp/data/constellation-fleet.json::apps[id=camera].release_url.

_doc_debug_api: #772 the routes this app adds to the fleet debug API (libs:devtools AppDebugServer): /api/<image_group>/recognize?route=ml|openrouter&path=<file> runs the shared image engine's recognize (libs:ml-l-image, contract 2) on a file this app can read, on the given route or the one More settings > Image recognition route holds, and reports the uniform result (labels with probabilities, boxes, text, colours, barcode, and whether it fell back to on-device).
_doc_debug_api_798: #798 /api/<image_group>/detect?path=<file>&mode=objects|labels|text runs live identification's detection (contract 3: boxes named by the full-label classifier, labels, text lines) on a file as a single photo; /api/<sound_group>/classify?ms=<n>|path=<wav>|test=tone|silence|noise identifies a sound through the shared sound engine (YAMNet) from the microphone, a WAV file or a synthetic test clip, and reports the labels, the timeline, the clip's peak and the engine's readiness.
_doc_debug_api_799: #799 /api/<image_group>/route[?set=openrouter|ml] and /api/<sound_group>/route[?set=] report the active recognition route per type (the user's; Model (Jev) by default), the declared default and the last route that answered (with fell_back and the reason); /api/<sound_group>/classify takes route= and reports the same. The rule is libs:ml-l-image RecognitionRoutes; the Sound route's Model half asks the decision model through the image engine.

web._doc: #876 Cloud Camera as a Kotlin/Wasm page (web/ is its own gradle root; the shared libs' pure-Compose sources arrive through the ab_cloud-libs-shared/web composite). Rendered into 1_cicd/src/cicd/ship-cloud-camera-wasm.yml by the workflow generator: `./gradlew wasmJsBrowserDistribution` in `dir`, tested by test/test-camera-web.sh, `build/dist/wasmJs/productionExecutable` zipped to `artifact` and attached to the rolling release as `gh_asset`. A mocked page: the island and tab strips are ui.bottom_nav / ui.sections as the Android shell reads them, the first section shows mock data and the rest say they live in the Android app. The APK's own ship ignores this directory.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh, which ship-cloud-camera.yml already invokes for shell/lint/unit — so this block is all that was needed to turn those three calls from 'SKIPPED LOUDLY' into real assertions. Before it, this app's green tick meant only that Gradle exited 0.

shell._doc_requires: python3 parses the layout and the manifest as XML rather than grepping them. A grep for an attribute also matches that attribute inside a comment, which is how a guard in this repository came to be satisfied by its own prose. Listed here so a runner without python3 REFUSES to run instead of reporting a verdict drawn from the interpreter's absence.

unit._doc: JVM tests of the pure logic: the nav / preview geometry (NavLayout), the detection overlay mapping, the filter anchor math and the declared-filters loading.

ui._doc: #868 THE nav declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl): ui.bottom_nav is the island, ui.sections[] what each item opens, ui.default_section where the app opens. The camera's MODES are the nav: the island carries the five families (QR Code | Objects | Camera | Video | VR) and the photo family's `pages` are the flavours a vendor extension may or may not offer at run time (ModeNav shows only the usable ones). Every id is the lower-cased CameraMode name (qr_scan, objects, auto, face_retouch, portrait, night, hdr, camera, video, vr), so the flat order below is the swipe order. The gallery's ViewPager is content, not nav.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: Private photos, video and QR scanning
about.description: Cloud Camera is the fleet's own signed build of GrapheneOS Camera, renamed so it can live next to an official copy. It takes photos and video with modern CameraX modes (auto, portrait, night, HDR, face retouch), scans QR and barcodes, and keeps everything in the phone's own gallery. It has no Play Services and no network calls of its own. It exists so the camera, one of the most privacy-sensitive apps, is built from audited source and updated by the fleet.
features: Photo modes: auto, portrait, night, HDR, face retouch
Everything stays in the phone's gallery
Objects: live on-device detection with boxes, labels, confidence and tracking ids
VR: face and object filters (hats, glasses, masks, backgrounds, colour looks, stickers)

screens.name: Objects
screens.what: Live on-device object detection with boxes, labels, confidence and tracking ids.

screens.name: VR
screens.what: Face and object filters (hats, glasses, masks, backgrounds, colour looks, stickers) on the live preview.

guide: Grant Camera (and Microphone for video) the first time.
Swipe between QR Code, Objects, Camera, Video and VR.
Tap the thumbnail to see the last shot in the gallery.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

related.why: Shows the photos and videos it takes.
Receives this app's crash reports on the phone.

about.credits: Upstream: GrapheneOS Camera (github.com/GrapheneOS/Camera), MIT licence, by the GrapheneOS project. The fleet build renames the package to cld.camera and adds the fleet's update and crash libraries.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
